why: path is passed through validatePath() (src/tools/filesystem.ts), which resolves symlinks via fs.realpath before the allowed-directory check so a symlink planted inside an allowed dir cannot redirect mkdir outside it.

file_path is resolved through the same validatePath()/isPathAllowed() guard used by every filesystem tool before any read/handler.editRange/writeFile call; old_string/new_string only rewrite content of that already-authorized file.

pid only matches terminalManager's own map of sessions it spawned via start_process (session.process.kill()); a pid for any other process is a no-op, so the argument never reaches an unrelated OS process.
takes only an optional 'origin' telemetry marker and returns the server's own config/system-info JSON; no caller-controlled path/command/injection surface.
filePath goes through validatePath() before fs.stat/getFileHandler, same allow-list+symlink-resolution guard as the other filesystem tools.
sessionId is only a lookup key into SearchManager's own in-memory session map of ripgrep processes it started; offset/length just slice an already-computed results array.
promptId is only used as an exact-match key into a bundled local JSON file (onboarding-prompts.json) to select which text to return; no path/command is derived from it.

maxResults/toolName/since only filter an in-memory array of the same session's own prior tool calls (toolHistory.ts); entries are JSON.stringify'd to disk, so no log-format/structured-log injection is possible.
GetUsageStatsArgsSchema is z.object({}) -- the tool takes no caller-controlled input at all.

GiveFeedbackArgsSchema is z.object({}); the only values placed into the shell command ('open "url"'/'xdg-open "url"') are server-generated stats and a UUID clientId, and URLSearchParams percent-encodes them before they reach exec(), so no caller input reaches the shell sink.

sending arbitrary input to a REPL/shell the caller itself started with start_process is this tool's whole declared purpose (its own description calls it the primary tool for driving REPLs/processes); it adds no privilege beyond what start_process already grants.

process.kill(pid) with no scoping is exactly what the tool's own description promises ('Terminate a running process by PID... use with caution'), unlike force_terminate which is explicitly scoped to server-managed sessions; behavior matches its declared contract.

the root path and every recursed subdirectory are each re-validated with validatePath()/isPathAllowed() before being read, so a symlink placed mid-tree cannot walk the listing outside the allowed directories.
ListProcessesArgsSchema is z.object({}); it just shells out to a fixed 'ps aux'/'tasklist' command with no caller-supplied data.
ListSearchesArgsSchema is z.object({}); it only enumerates SearchManager's own in-memory sessions.
ListSessionsArgsSchema is z.object({}); it only enumerates terminalManager's own in-memory sessions.
both source and destination are independently resolved through validatePath()/isPathAllowed() before fs.rename(), same guard as the rest of the filesystem tools.

local reads go through validatePath(); the isUrl branch fetches whatever URL the caller supplies, which is the tool's own advertised feature ('Can fetch content from URLs') with no extra twist -- verified the installed node-fetch@2.7.0 used by cross-fetch@4.1.0 (node_modules/node-fetch/lib/index.js: 'Only HTTP(S) protocols are supported') rejects any non-http(s) scheme, so isUrl cannot be used as a file:// read to bypass allowedDirectories.
each path in the array is independently passed through validatePath() before being read; a failure on one path is caught per-file and does not affect validation of the others.
pid only selects among terminalManager's own tracked sessions/completed-session buffers; offset/length just paginate an already-buffered output array.

key is checked against an explicit allow-list (isConfigFieldKey/CONFIG_FIELD_DEFINITIONS: blockedCommands, allowedDirectories, defaultShell, telemetryEnabled, fileReadLineLimit, fileWriteLineLimit) before any write; every resulting effect, including allowedDirectories=[] granting full-disk access, is the tool's own documented behavior, not an unintended bypass.

running the caller's command string in a real shell is this tool's entire declared purpose ('Start a new terminal process'); commandManager.validateCommand()'s blocklist is a best-effort supplementary safety net, not the security boundary, so its bypassability does not itself constitute a finding per the anti-false-positive rule for advertised command-execution tools.

path is validated with validatePath() before ripgrep runs; pattern/filePattern are passed as discrete argv entries to spawn(rgPath, args) with no shell:true, so no command injection is possible, and ripgrep's Rust regex engine is not vulnerable to catastrophic-backtracking ReDoS.
sessionId only selects among SearchManager's own tracked ripgrep child processes to send SIGTERM to; it cannot reference any other process.
path is resolved through validatePath()/isPathAllowed() before getFileHandler().write(), same guard as the rest of the filesystem tools.

sink: md-to-pdf@5.2.5 merges this config with zero key allow-list, then convertMdToPdf() does fs.promises.writeFile(config.dest, pdfBytes) and generateOutput() does puppeteer.launch(config.launch_options) plus page.addScriptTag({url})/addStyleTag({url}) for each config.script/stylesheet entry
why: write_pdf's own 'options' argument is z.object({}).passthrough() (src/tools/schemas.ts WritePdfArgsSchema, comment 'Allow passing options to md-to-pdf') and is forwarded verbatim through src/tools/pdf/markdown.ts:302 (mdToPdf({content: markdown}, options)) into md-to-pdf's internal config with no key filtering. Read the installed md-to-pdf@5.2.5 source directly: convertMdToPdf() also merges any YAML front-matter found inside the caller-supplied markdown 'content' straight into that same config object (config = Object.assign({}, config, frontMatterConfig, {pdf_options:...})), so the same override is reachable purely through 'content' even if 'options' is omitted. Either route lets the caller set config.dest to an arbitrary absolute path; md-to-pdf's own convertMdToPdf() then runs fs.promises.writeFile(output.filename, output.content) with that path, completely bypassing this server's validatePath()/allowedDirectories check, which src/tools/filesystem.ts writePdf() only ever applies to its own path/outputPath/sourcePdfPath parameters -- never to options.dest or a front-matter dest. The tool's own description states 'Only works within allowed directories', which this route falsifies. The same unrestricted merge also lets the caller set launch_options (passed straight into puppeteer.launch() in generate-output.js) and script/stylesheet entries (loaded via page.addScriptTag({url:<attacker URL>})/addStyleTag), giving outbound SSRF from the server host plus execution of attacker-hosted JavaScript inside the rendering page -- confirmed by reading the installed dependency's code, not assumed from its reputation.
